previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis complicated by cirrhosis was admitted with recurrent cholangitis, presenting with fever and right upper quadrant pain. She had recently completed a course of ciprofloxacin but developed symptoms consistent with a flare. Imaging confirmed a persistent 7mm stone in the right intrahepatic duct, which could not be removed due to anatomical constraints. She was treated with intravenous meropenem, transitioned to ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line for a 14-day course, and showed clinical and laboratory improvement. Chronic medications were managed, with lisinopril and furosemide held initially and restarted at discharge. She was discharged home with home health support for IV antibiotics and plans for outpatient MRCP and gastroenterology follow-up.

PROCEDURES: ============== ERCP ___ Findings: Esophagus:Limited exam of the esophagus was normal Stomach:Limited exam of the stomach was normal Duodenum:Limited exam of the duodenum was normal Major Papilla:Evidence of a previous sphincterotomy was noted in the major papilla. Cannulation:Cannulation of the biliary duct was successful and deep with a sphincterotome using a free-hand technique. Contrast medium was injected resulting in complete opacification. Fluoroscopic Interpretation of Biliary Tree:Scout film revealed the previous CCY clips in the right upper quadrant. The common bile duct, common hepatic duct, right and left hepatic ducts, and biliary radicles were filled with contrast and well visualized. There was a filling defect that appeared like sludge in the common hepatic duct. The intrahepatic ducts showed mutliple strictures and dilations consistent with the patient's known primary sclerosing cholangitis. No strictures or abnormalities were appreciated in the common bile duct. Fluoroscopic Interpretation:I supervised the acquisition and interpretation of the fluoroscopic images. The quality of the fluoroscopic images was good. Total fluoroscopy time: 7.1 minutes. Procedures:A small amount of sludge was extracted successfully using sweeps of the extraction balloon. Given the imaging findings showing a biliary stone and the patient's recurrent episodes of cholangitis, the decision was made to perform sphincteroplasty followed by Spyglass cholangioscopy for further evaluation. Balloon sphincteroplasty was successfully performed using a 10mm wire-guided CRE balloon that was introduced for dilation of the biliary sphincter. Spyglass cholangioscopy was performed. An embedded stone was identified at the common hepatic duct. There appeared to biliary mucosa overgrowing the embedded stone. Given this finding, the decision was made to use Spybite biopsies to attempt to dislodge the embedded stone. Multiple Spybite cold forceps biopsies were performed for histology at the common hepatic duct. After several rounds of biopsies, a portion of the embedded stone appeared to become dislodged. Therefore, the decision was made to repeat balloon sweep. A portion of stone and possible biliary tissue were extracted successfully using a sweep of the extraction balloon. MRCP was performed demonstrating a 5 mm filling defect within the common hepatic duct, which most likely representing an obstructive stone. ERCP was subsequently performed and an embedded stone was identified at the common hepatic duct with biliary mucosa overgrowing the stone. Biopsies of the stone and overlying tissue were taken, and at least a portion of the stone was dislodged and cleared with sweeping of the biliary tree. radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with PSC and fever/RUQ pain // eval for stone,
duct dilation

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The echogenicity of the liver is homogeneous. The contour of the liver
is smooth. There is no focal liver mass. Main portal vein is patent with
hepatopetal flow. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 7 mm
and appears slightly thickened consistent with the provided diagnosis of
primary sclerosing cholangitis. No stones are visualized within the common
bile duct. As per the prior ultrasound report a retained stone measuring 1.3
cm is seen within the central intrahepatic ducts possibly within the trunk of
the right hepatic duct. There is no upstream intrahepatic biliary duct
dilation.

GALLBLADDER: Surgically absent.

PANCREAS: Head, body and tail of the pancreas are within normal limits,
without masses or pancreatic ductal dilatation.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

As per the prior report there is retained stone in the central intrahepatic
ducts, possibly located in the trunk of the right hepatic duct. There is no
upstream intrahepatic biliary dilation. No stones are identified within the
common bile duct.

NOTIFICATION:  Findings were placed on the Dashboard by ___ at 17:03 on ___.

EXAMINATION:  MRCP

INDICATION:  PSC and chronic recurrent cholangitis, planning for possible
ERCP.  Assess biliary system for stones, dilatation, and cholangitis. 
Planning for ERCP.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar, multisequential MRI of the abdomen with MRCP was
performed at pre and post the uneventful administration of 6 mL of Gadavist
intravenous contrast.

COMPARISON:  Compared with previous MRI abdomen from ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is irregular nodular intrahepatic bile ducts (9:1) with atrophy of
segments within the left and right hepatic lobes compatible with known primary
sclerosing cholangitis; the overall appearance is similar when compared to the
prior examination. There is mild hyperenhancement of the intrahepatic bile
ducts and common bile duct which is overall similar when compared to the prior
examination and also in keeping with primary sclerosing cholangitis.  There
are no findings to suggest acute cholangitis.

There is a 5 mm filling defect within the common hepatic duct, which most
probably represents an obstructive stone (9:1).  Again noted is high
termination of the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct which may reflect
sphincter of Oddi dysfunction (3:28).

The liver demonstrates diffuse heterogeneous appearance on T2 weighted images
within the right and left lower lobe with areas of confluent fibrosis, overall
similar to previous.  The portal vein is patent.

The adrenal glands, kidneys, pancreas, appear unremarkable.  There has been
prior cholecystectomy.  There is mild splenomegaly with the spleen measuring
up to 13.8 cm.  There is no upper intra-abdominal or retroperitoneal
lymphadenopathy.

The lung bases appear unremarkable.

The bone marrow signal intensity is within normal lumen limits.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  5 mm filling defect within the common hepatic duct, which most probably
represents an obstructive stone

2.  Confluent hepatic fibrosis and irregular intrahepatic bile ducts with
hepatic atrophy in keeping with known primary sclerosing cholangitis similar
to the prior examination from ___.

3.  High termination the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct which may
reflect Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction.

4.  Mild splenomegaly.
